reviewer: Claude review agent (independent of the extractor); no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the POISK batch by a different agent from the extractor, against the extraction frozen at batch.jsonl SHA-256 4a99cc8675bffe91ddbc7d75a8d23bc94b2447508d44e3ad4014cec66540b694 (221 records: 5 sources, 3 models, 1 method, 8 configurations, 2 datasets, 3 dataset subsets, 1 benchmark, 1 task, 13 protocols, 66 evaluations, 78 results, 40 claims). The reviewed batch holds 229 records, the 8 added being metadata-correction claims written by this review. All five pinned artifacts were re-retrieved on 2026-11-16. The two Zenodo API responses (records 19883049 and 21775623), the explorer page and the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML each hashed to the value on their source record. The v1 PDF did not: three downloads gave 3389c1bf6d3654c5b2151a07fcfcefc67cf6f36e5f0facfc03c33521d8b84491 twice and d699fd680e3b0097ca80130c288e8d872773dc1e523044f4605e06fc4f89d9bc once, none equal to the recorded 526def150fb5ae8f9ac4533efcf16c86e547e636cdb9bfba9a574cd1e2a2f924, because bioRxiv regenerates the container on request. A pdftotext -layout run (poppler 26.08.0) on all three downloads gave the same text layer, SHA-256 e75c18130ca43770d2f0ed05ae96528759666c0e4fa08f7725f5a32b21187696, byte for byte the contents of the archived artifacts/biorxiv-v1-layout.txt.gz, so the archive is provably derived from the pinned article and is the artifact every value was verified against. The recorded artifact_sha256 was left as it stands and the finding is recorded on the source record (hash_scope, a limitation, review_artifact and review_artifact_matches_original_artifact_sha256 false) and in metadata-correction-e15a67f34f1001960b98. npm run batch -- check-values was rerun against the regenerated text layer and reproduced the extractor's figures exactly (36 in_cell, 36 in_row, 6 locator_not_parsed, no not_in_row, no wrong_column, no overclaimed_in_row), writing a value-check.tsv byte-identical to the extractor's. All 78 results were then re-read by review/check_values_independent.py, written for this pass and importing nothing from extract/build_batch.py: it takes each table's column spans from the character offsets of the label text in that table's own printed header lines, assigns every numeric token on a body row to the column whose centre is nearest, and rejects a row unless the token count matches the column count, the nearest column is the one in the token's own left-to-right position, and the runner-up column loses by at least three characters; it also asserts that Table 1's four sub-columns sit under their group labels, that Table 7's Coverage group spans the five coverage columns and does not reach the Ties column, and that Table 8's body holds exactly 27 construct rows. Records are matched to cells through each result's source_locator text, not its ID. 72 results were checked in cell, which includes all 36 that check-values could only place at row level, and the 6 prose values were checked against the sentence each locator names and against which engine or setting that sentence attaches each value to. Two negative controls confirmed the checker fails as intended: swapping the Protenix-v2 and Boltz-2 Table 7 50% values is caught (review/control-swap.tsv), and so is shifting the AlphaFold-Multimer Table 7 50% cell to its 75% neighbour's value 0.643 and the Boltz-2 Table 2 cell to the row below's 56.5 (review/control-shift.tsv), both of which a row-level check passes because the value is present in the row. Independently of any script, all 42 printed cells of Tables 2 and 7 were transcribed by hand into review/manual-transcription.tsv and compared with the records by review/cmp_manual.py: every cell matched, covering column assignment for each of the 36 cells the extractor left unverified, and Table 2's printed row order, which ascends by recovery rate and is not the row order of Tables 1 and 7, was read off the page rather than assumed. review/audit_fields.py checked every result's metric, direction, unit and denominator against its protocol and every evaluation's nine comparison fields for completeness. Version 2 of the preprint, posted 2026-11-14 and inside the search window, was retrieved (PDF SHA-256 aeaec593d7aa2d42382a49bd6fadbbccabaa6c084843ea1c7f0c91097dedb0c2, text layer SHA-256 82a99bc2e061b7247cf65f7bc9450924b7af5be7ab3ef283d2284ba787ea629c): every numeric token in it is identical to version 1's apart from an added author affiliation and the two Zenodo record identifiers, so no stored value changes and the batch stays pinned to version 1. The 40 descriptive claims were read against the pinned PDF text layer, both re-retrieved Zenodo API responses and the re-retrieved explorer page. Rulings, including the three protocols whose metric_implementation described a scoring step their endpoint does not use, are in docs/reviews/2026-11-16-poisk.md.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude agent, independent of the extractor but not human scientific review. Transcription was checked against the pinned source; nothing was reproduced and no value was recomputed from data.

The pinned v1 PDF's artifact_sha256 does not reproduce. bioRxiv regenerates the container on request, so no refetch will ever match it and the hash cannot serve as a verification anchor. The anchor this review used instead is the pdftotext -layout text layer, SHA-256 e75c18130ca43770d2f0ed05ae96528759666c0e4fa08f7725f5a32b21187696, which three independent downloads reproduced and which is archived under archive_sha256. notes.md's statement that the PDF was downloaded twice with identical bytes is contradicted by this review.

No POISK data file was downloaded, by the extractor or by this review. The two release tables, the 47-column schema file, the extractor and auditor prompts and all folding artifacts are unhashed. Nothing in the batch rests on their contents and nothing was recomputed from the released per-complex metrics, so the file-level claims rest on the Zenodo records' own file lists, which do carry sizes and md5 values.

The ipSAE scoring tool is not pinned. The paper names "a modified implementation of the ipSAE tool" at https://github.com/DunbrackLab/IPSAE with no commit, tag or released code, so no snapshot would describe what ran and the published values cannot be recomputed. No evidence concern was added: metric_implementation is a comparison field, it is populated on all 66 evaluations with the modification named, so an automatic comparison against another study's ipSAE figure is already blocked, and within the batch all six engines were scored by the same implementation, which is the comparison the batch supports. The gap is recorded as a limitation on every affected evaluation and in claim-ipsae-definition.

Table 8's 162 per-construct cells and all 132 cells of Table 6 stay unextracted, with reasons in scope-audit.jsonl. This review accepted both exclusions rather than widening the batch; both are retrievable from the same pinned artifact. Figure 5's 36 error bars, top-5 retrieval for every engine and top-10 retrieval for four of the six engines print no numbers and remain gaps.

The negatives are putative. No result in the batch is a measured binding event, a measured non-binding event or an affinity, and the ipSAE and ipTM figures are structural confidence scores used for ranking. This review confirmed the statement is carried on the benchmark record, the benchmark subset, all 66 evaluations and the relevant claims.

The store already holds OpenFold3 as an unparented configuration, esmfold2-2026-runs-n-poses-method-openfold3-msa, whose links array is empty. The new family record poisk-20261115-model-openfold3 is correct and the pointer is recorded in its provenance_note, but the family edge on that existing configuration was not added, because it changes a stored record outside this batch. It is left for the coordinator.

No discrepancies file is present in the worktree and none of this batch's results is in the store yet, so there was nothing for the discrepancy step to settle. Any lead the knowledge-graph build raises after the merge is unreviewed.
